title: Observability’s Stakeholders and Allies
subtitle: Help adjacent teams answer their own questions
summary: Pip’s support colleague has a customer request the dashboards missed. Different stakeholders need different outcomes from telemetry. Detailed operational exploration can inform product and account decisions, but sampled evidence must not masquerade as an exact billing ledger.

concepts.title: Support can identify customer impact
concepts.body: Pip receives a specific failed request from support. Request context establishes whether the issue continues, which workflow failed, and whether it belongs to a broader incident. A useful investigation path makes escalation precise. Pip gives support evidence rather than another vague service-status update.

concepts.title: Product and success compare actual use
concepts.body: Pip sees feature uptake rise but checkout completion remain poor. Event sequences and attributes reveal attempted paths, failures, and demo-only use. Product and customer-success teams can compare relevant cohorts before and after guidance or changes. Pip tests whether customers achieve their goals instead of counting activation alone.

concepts.title: Allies need their own useful outcomes
concepts.body: Pip’s account team needs to know which feature a renewing customer actually depends on. Sales and leaders gain allies’ reasons to invest when telemetry answers decisions about usage and performance. Project updates alone do not create that usefulness. Pip translates observed workflows into priorities without replacing evidence with stakeholder enthusiasm.

concepts.title: Operational exploration is not accounting
concepts.body: Pip nearly calculates an invoice from sampled requests. Operational exploration values fresh, fast answers and may trade accuracy through sampling or incomplete scans. Accounting may require exact totals and longer history. Pip uses telemetry to investigate behavior and connects complementary systems without silently promoting estimates into a billing ledger.

misconceptions.claim: Stakeholders become allies merely by receiving project updates.
misconceptions.correction: They become active supporters when the capability helps solve their own concrete problems.

misconceptions.claim: A fast observability query is automatically suitable for exact billing.
misconceptions.correction: Sampling and other approximation trade-offs may make a separate authoritative accounting source necessary.

scenario.title: The sales dashboard counts demos as adoption
scenario.context: A heavily demonstrated feature appears popular, but customer success sees little regular use.

options.label: Compare demo traffic with real workflow cohorts
options.benefit: Tests whether the usage supports the adoption claim.
options.cost: Requires context that distinguishes origins and outcomes.
options.consequence: Product and success teams can distinguish interest during demonstrations from continuing use.

options.label: Report the total call count as product success
options.cost: Conflates demonstrations with successful customer workflows.
options.consequence: The organization may invest on the basis of activity that does not represent adoption.

scenario.debrief: A stakeholder question often needs request context beyond a convenient aggregate.

quiz.question: Which first step is most likely to win a support team’s participation?
options: Help answer a recurring customer-specific failure question
quiz.explanation: A useful outcome in the team’s own workflow creates a practical reason to participate.

quiz.question: Why might an observability dataset be unsuitable as the sole billing source?
options: It may contain sampled or approximate results rather than exact totals
Any request-level data must be aggregated monthly before it can be accurate
Grouping by account removes the need to account for different sampling rates
quiz.explanation: Operational speed and cost choices do not automatically meet accounting accuracy requirements.

quiz.question: A feature has many calls but little customer value. What could clarify this?
options: Counting the same total more frequently
Examining whether calls complete useful workflows or only occur in demos
Treating the number of feature calls as the number of completed user goals
quiz.explanation: Context and sequences help distinguish activity from meaningful use.
